newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says will not meet US travel ban terms.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says will not meet US travel ban terms.

text.p: A Hizbollah leader on Tuesday condemned the U.S. decision to lift its travel ban on Americans visiting Lebanon and said the pro-Iranian group would not abide by its conditions on terrorism.

"We will stand with our brothers in parliament against the draft terrorism law which the United States claims to be part of the deal for lifting the ban," deputy secretary-general of Hizbollah Naee'm Kassem told a crowd of thousands of supporters at a funeral procession of four Hizbollah fighters killed by Israeli forces on Monday.
Kassem said the U.S. decision to lift the ban was based on self-interest.
Hizbollah supporters chanted "Death of America" as Kassem questioned the motives of the U.S. move.

Last Wednesday, U.S. Secretary of State Madeline Albright lifted the 10-year-old ban after Lebanon pledged to fight "terrorism" and sign a convention to work with Washington in any hostage-taking cases.
